moduleTitle: Lesson 3 - Retrieving and Updating Test records through TDS
learningObjectives: Retrieve a specific test record using 'TestData - Find & provide record' and an ActionMode Constraint.
Write the {TD[ObjectName.AttributeName]} expression to feed retrieved data into a TestStepValue.
Update a test record's Status using 'TestData - Update record', understanding that updates always pair with a search.
Move consumed records into a new TDS type using 'TestData - Move record to TDS type'.

elements.description: Retrieves a previously created record via a search query. The 'Existing TDS type*' field defines which dataset to search (e.g. CustomerDetails).
Restricts the search to records matching a specific condition — e.g. TDS attribute Status = 'New', to find only newly registered customers rather than any customer record.

elements.text: Because this course's scenario has only one user type (the customer) and no Alias name was set in Lesson 2, Tosca automatically uses the 'Existing TDS type*' value itself to search — it looks in the CustomerDetails dataset for a record with Status = New.

bulletPoints: Existing TDS type* = which dataset to search. ActionMode Constraint = which record(s) within it.

elements.description: Once a record is found, its values are fed into the SUT using the {TD[...]} expression, entered directly in a TestStepValue's Value field — the same style of expression used elsewhere in the Automation Specialist courses. The part right after the opening brace is the command to retrieve a test record from the TDS repository; the part in square brackets identifies exactly which value, as TDSType.AttributeName.

To log a newly registered customer into the DemoWebShop using their retrieved email address, the Value field would contain: {TD[CustomerDetails.Email]} — retrieve a record from the CustomerDetails type and use its Email attribute.

bulletPoints: {TD[ObjectName.AttributeName]} — TDS type first, then the specific Attribute, separated by a full stop.

elements.description: Used whenever a record's data needs to change — e.g. once a newly registered customer adds an address, their Status should move from New to Active. Updating a record in TDS always works together with a search: you must first find the correct record, then apply the update to it.

The TestStepValue 'Existing alias name (record)*' on the Update module must match the value used earlier when the record was searched for — in this example, 'CustomerDetails'. The update itself targets a TDS attribute (Status) and supplies its new value (Active, replacing New).

elements.text: Once the TestCase runs, the Status change is immediately visible in the TDS repository.

bulletPoints: No standalone 'blind update' — every update is preceded by a matching find/search.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: How the repository evolves through the order process

elements.title: Status/column changes as the customer journey progresses
items: Adding items to the cart → an 'items' column appears showing the count.
Purchasing items → creates an OrderNumber column, sets OrderStatus to Pending.
Processing the purchase order → OrderStatus changes to Processing.

elements.description: Step 1 (backend): non-UI Standard Modules search for a record with OrderStatus = Pending, then send non-UI requests carrying that OrderID plus the customer's email and password to the backend. Tosca verifies a 200 OK response, confirming the payment succeeded — this moves the status to Processing in the backend system itself, but NOT yet in TDS. Step 2 (repository sync): Tosca searches again for that same Pending-OrderStatus record, verifies the DemoWebShop now shows it as Processing, and only then updates the TDS repository's copy of that record to Processing.

elements.text: The backend status and the TDS repository status change in two separate steps — don't assume TDS updates itself automatically just because the backend changed.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Moving consumed records to a new TDS type

elements.description: Once the full order process (including payment) has run, that customer's data is considered consumed. Moving it into a distinct TDS type keeps the repository stateful — it's immediately clear which records are still 'live' and which have already been used, which is especially valuable for a distributed team.

elements.term: TestData - Move record to TDS type
elements.description: Searches for records under the existing TDS type (e.g. CustomerDetails) and relocates them to a new type under a new name (e.g. CustomerDetails_Used). The TestStepValue 'Existing alias name (record)*' takes the CURRENT type's value (CustomerDetails), while 'Existing or new TDS type*' takes the DESTINATION type's value (CustomerDetails_Used).

bulletPoints: 'Existing alias name (record)*' = where the record is coming FROM. 'Existing or new TDS type*' = where it's going TO.

examPitfalls.title: Trying to update a record without searching for it first
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Adding a 'TestData - Update record' module and expecting it to know which record to change without a matching search.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Updating in TDS always works in conjunction with a search — the 'Existing alias name (record)*' value on the Update module must match how the record was originally found.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming payment status syncs to TDS automatically
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Believing that once the backend confirms payment (200 OK, status → Processing), the TDS repository is updated at the same moment.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Payment processing is a deliberate two-step flow: first the backend status changes via non-UI requests, THEN a separate search+update step syncs that same change into the TDS repository.

examPitfalls.title: Mixing up the two TDS type fields on Move record
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Putting the destination type name into 'Existing alias name (record)*' instead of 'Existing or new TDS type*'.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: 'Existing alias name (record)*' = the CURRENT type the record is being moved FROM. 'Existing or new TDS type*' = the type it's being moved TO.

examPitfalls.title: Getting the {TD[...]} argument order backwards
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The syntax is always TDSType.AttributeName — the TDS type comes first, then the specific attribute, separated by a full stop.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester wants to log a newly registered customer into the DemoWebShop using their stored email address, TDS type 'CustomerDetails'. What expression goes in the TestStepValue's Value field?
practiceQuiz.hint: TDS type comes first, then the attribute, joined by a period.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The correct syntax is {TD[ObjectName.AttributeName]} — TDS type first, then the Attribute, separated by a full stop: {TD[CustomerDetails.Email]}.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester adds 'TestData - Update record' to change a customer's Status from New to Active, but the module has no way to know which specific record to change. What's missing?

options.text: A preceding search/find step that identifies the target record, matched via 'Existing alias name (record)*'.

practiceQuiz.hint: Updating in TDS is never a standalone action.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Updating a TDS record always pairs with a search — the Update module's 'Existing alias name (record)*' must match the identity used when the record was originally found, so Tosca knows exactly which record to change.

practiceQuiz.scenario: During payment processing, Tosca gets a 200 OK response from the backend and the payment status becomes Processing there. Is the TDS repository automatically updated at this point?

options.text: Yes, TDS always mirrors backend status changes instantly.
No — a separate step must search for the same Pending record, confirm it now shows Processing in the DemoWebShop, and then explicitly update the TDS repository.
Only if Repetitions is set to 1.

practiceQuiz.hint: Payment processing is described as a deliberate two-step flow.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The backend status change and the TDS repository update are two distinct steps — TDS is only updated once Tosca separately searches for the record, confirms the new state, and applies the update.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester wants to move all fully-processed records from 'CustomerDetails' into a new type called 'CustomerDetails_Used'. Which value goes into 'Existing or new TDS type*' on the Move record module?
practiceQuiz.hint: One field is the source type, the other is the destination.
practiceQuiz.rationale: 'Existing alias name (record)*' takes the CURRENT type (CustomerDetails); 'Existing or new TDS type*' takes the DESTINATION type — CustomerDetails_Used.

quickRecap.value: TestData - Find & provide record; Existing TDS type* + ActionMode Constraint narrow the search.
{TD[ObjectName.AttributeName]} — TDS type, then Attribute, separated by a full stop.
TestData - Update record — always paired with a matching search (Existing alias name (record)*).
Backend status change (non-UI, 200 OK) happens first; TDS repository update is a separate, later step.
TestData - Move record to TDS type — 'Existing alias name (record)*' = FROM, 'Existing or new TDS type*' = TO.
